title: How the signature timestamp prints on a signed note

claims.claim: The Provider Attestation block on every signed progress note prints when the note was signed and in which timezone.

checks.note: renderer is live in the wizard

claims.claim: For a signed note, the timestamp line reads like: Aug 25, 2026, 11:07 PM EDT
The date is the calendar day of signing, not the date of service; when the two differ, the signing day is what prints.
The time is hour and minute, no seconds.
The timezone abbreviation is always printed.

checks.pattern: date-only, no time  -> the calendar day alone
checks.note: a bare-date value prints the day with no zone

claims.finding: A signature value stored as a bare YYYY-MM-DD prints the day alone with no zone (formatters.ts:253-257 at v1.1.345); every value with a time prints the abbreviation.
claims.proposed_text: The timezone abbreviation is printed whenever the signature was recorded with a time, which is every signature made in the Visit Wizard.

proposed_checks.pattern: date-only, no time  -> the calendar day alone

claims.claim: The timestamp prints in the timezone of the device that generates the PDF, not in the facility's timezone; regenerating from a device in another zone gives a different reading of the same instant.
For an unsigned note the line reads "Not recorded"; Medipyxis never prints a substitute signature date.

checks.note: only the comment recording the removed fallback remains

claims.claim: The device clock is chosen because it needs no supporting data to be right; the zone abbreviation makes every printed copy a self-describing statement of the same instant.

checks.pattern: device clock needs no data to be correct.

claims.claim: Near midnight, two US timezones can disagree on the calendar day; both copies are correct.

checks.pattern: window where two US timezones disagree on the calendar day

claims.claim: Both copies are generated from the same stored instant, each rendered in the timezone of the device that requested the download.
The signature timestamp is written when the provider clicks Sign in step 17 of the Visit Wizard.
claims.finding: signed_at is written when the provider clicks Complete Provider Attestation in step 17 (ProviderAttestationVisit.tsx:346, button at :818 at v1.1.345); Sign & Lock comes later in the review window.
claims.proposed_text: The signature timestamp is written when the provider clicks Complete Provider Attestation in step 17 of the Visit Wizard.

claims.claim: If the timestamp does not appear, check that the note is actually signed — a locked note is not the same as a signed note.
claims.finding: In the product, signed means Sign & Lock ran (visitSignState.ts:5 at v1.1.345), so locked and signed are the same; the printed timestamp comes from the step 17 attestation (s15_attestation.ts:214).
claims.proposed_text: If the line reads Not recorded, Provider Attestation was not completed in step 17. The timestamp comes from the attestation; Sign & Lock then signs and locks the visit in one step.
